Expand cell-level data into triangle polygon coordinates

Source: R/data-transform.R
build_triangles.Rd

Internal helper shared by the clutch renderer and geom_biheat(). Given a data frame of cell centres, returns a long data frame of polygon vertices suitable for grid::polygonGrob() or ggplot2::geom_polygon(). Two polygons are produced per input row: one for the upper-value triangle and one for the lower-value triangle.

Usage

build_triangles(data, split = c("down", "up"), inset = 0)

Arguments

data

A data frame with numeric x, y (cell centres) and upper, lower (cell values). Optional numeric width and height columns give per-cell footprints; both default to 1.

split

One of "down" (top-left to bottom-right diagonal) or "up" (bottom-left to top-right diagonal).

inset

Numeric in [0, 0.5). Shrinks each cell's footprint by this fraction of its width and height on every side, opening a gap between neighbouring cells. 0 gives contiguous cells; 0.04 gives an ~8% gap.

Value

A data frame with columns x, y, polygon_id, which, value, .row (the index of the source row in data).

Details

Coordinates follow the display convention, so y grows upward: for split = "down" the cell is cut from its top-left to its bottom-right corner and the upper triangle is the one above that cut.
